mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more indicates weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 falls by 2% or more year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% over three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of three-month INDPRO decline exceeding 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive correlation between HOUST (new single-family houses started) and INDPRO over the past six months indicates synchronized growth in housing and industrial activity, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when the 6-month correlation between HOUST and INDPRO exceeds 0.7.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 250k per month for two consecutive months signals a robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 250000 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during episodes of two consecutive months with PAYEMS growth above 250k.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals reduced household buffer and higher consumption financed by debt, which temporarily supports consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods when RSAFS is below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months.
